what: Validation-methodology preference (2026-04-26): when validating safety-net mechanisms (hard-blocks, deny enforcement, fallback paths), do NOT settle for "the happy path passes therefore the safety net would work if needed." FORCE the adversarial scenario explicitly — i.e., construct conditions where the safety net MUST fire. Concrete techniques: (a) instruct the agent explicitly to skip the proactive guidance ("Do NOT call aide_recall. Just use the Read tool directly."), (b) use clean tracking state so no prior covering exists, (c) test in a fresh session to avoid context carryover. Without forcing the adversarial path, you only validate that agents follow good guidance — not that the safety net catches them when they don't. This applies to: hard-block deny enforcement (Cursor #154377 still untested if agent always recalls first), correction-detection fallback paths, retry-after-deny flows. Complements memories #341 (test isolation via fresh session) + #342 (use agent-facing channel). Together: fresh session + agent-facing path + adversarial instructions = trustworthy validation.
why: User pushback during Cursor A1 validation (2026-04-26): "but want to test the block flow, not just oh it will work if it happens." I had marked A1 as PASS via the proactive-recall path and was tempted to call the hard-block validated by extension. User rightly insisted on FORCING the adversarial scenario where agent skips recall — without that, we never actually verified Cursor honors `permission: deny`. Storing as guideline so future validation walks (other editors, future safety-net mechanisms) include explicit adversarial test variants rather than relying on happy-path coverage. Critical for any "fail-safe" claim in product marketing or release docs.
